In 2004 Transparency International tried to rank history's biggest embezzlers. The man at the top allegedly stole more than the entire annual budget of the country he ran.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Suharto, Indonesia, 1967-1998: $15-35 billion. Transparency International's Global Corruption Report ranked him the most corrupt head of government it could document — the largest single figure on the whole list.

2/ Marcos, Philippines, 1965-1986: $5-10 billion, much of it routed through shell companies into Swiss accounts. Switzerland froze $658 million of it, and the Philippine Supreme Court didn't win it back for the treasury until 2003-2004.

3/ Mobutu, Zaire, 1965-1997: TI put it at $4-5 billion. He chartered a Concorde from Air France for Paris shopping trips and built an airport at his home village of Gbadolite long enough to land one, while state salaries went unpaid for months.

4/ Abacha, Nigeria, 1993-1998: $2-5 billion in just five years, the fastest pace on this list. Nigeria is still chasing it — $3.65 billion recovered by 2022, most of it from Swiss banks, with more still being negotiated today.

5/ Add up the four estimates and you get roughly $60 billion taken from four countries that are still fighting poverty their own leaders helped cause. The documented recoveries alone are damning enough without rounding anything up.
